body.p: In response to the office action dated September 6, 2024, Applicant has amended independent claims 16 and 26. Claim 19 has been canceled. Claims 1-15 were previously cancelled. Claims 16-35 are presented for examination. No new matter has been added. Support for the claim amendments can be found throughout the application as filed.

Applicant thanks Examiner Wu for the indication that claims 19, 23 and 29-30 recite allowable subject matter. Applicant has amended independent claims 16 and 26 to incorporate the allowable subject matter of claim 19. Therefore, allowance of all claims is respectfully requested.
Non-Statutory Obviousness-type Double Patenting

Claims 16-35 stand provisionally rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness- type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-13 of U.S. Patent No. 11,426,108. In addition, claims 16-35 stand provisionally rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,857,325.

Without conceding to the Office's position and in an effort to advance prosecution of the instant application, Applicant has amended each of the independent claims 16 and 26 to incorporate the allowable subject matter of claim 19. In particular, independent claim 16 has been amended to recite: "wherein the supplementary device is configured to be releasably attached over a button of the injection device, and the sensor is configured to measure a position or a movement of the button." Independent claim 26 has been amended to recite: "wherein the supplementary device is configured to be releasably attached over a button of the injection device, and the first sensor is configured to measure a position or a movement of the button."
None of the granted claims of U.S. Patent No. 11,426,108 and U.S. Patent No.

11,857,325 has the above amended features of independent claims 16 and 26. In addition, the Office acknowledges that claim 19 includes allowable subject matter, which implies that the above amended features are novel. Therefore, with the above amended features, the amended
independent claims 16 and 26 and their respective dependent claims are patentably distinct from claims 1-13 of U.S. Patent No. 11,426,108 and claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,857,325.
Accordingly, withdrawal of the non-statutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection and allowance of the pending application are respectfully requested.
Claims 16-18, 20-21,27, 31-32 and 34-35 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Hochman, U.S. Publication No. 2009/0030366 ("Hochman").
Claims 22, 24, 28 and 33 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being
unpatentable over Hochman in view of Kim et al., U.S. Publication No. 2013/0226372 ("Kim").

Without conceding to the Office's position and in an effort to advance prosecution of the instant application, Applicant has amended each of the independent claims 16 and 26 to incorporate the allowable subject matter of claim 19. In particular, independent claim 16 has been amended to recite: "wherein the supplementary device is configured to be releasably attached over a button of the injection device, and the sensor is configured to measure a position or a movement of the button." Independent claim 26 has been amended to recite similar features. Accordingly, claim 19 has been canceled.
Therefore, claims 16 and 26 are allowable. Withdrawal of the rejections and allowance of all claims are respectfully requested.
For the foregoing reasons, Applicant submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance.

By responding in the foregoing remarks only to particular positions taken in the action, the applicant does not acquiesce with other positions that have not been explicitly addressed. In addition, the Applicant's selecting some particular arguments for the patentability of a claim should not be understood as implying that no other reasons for the patentability of that claim exist. Finally, the Applicant's decision to amend or cancel any claim should not be understood as implying that the Applicant agrees with any positions taken in the action with reference to that claim or other claims, or that the Applicant adopts or agrees with any position except as
specifically stated in this paper. In particular, by amending a claim, the Applicant does not necessarily concede that the claim prior to amendment was unpatentable.
